rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parables serve clear instruction, a distinctive feature of this law, by making abstract meanings easier to grasp.
rows.anchor: ومن حكمته تعليم البيان وهو من خصائص هذه الشريعة والمثل أعون شىء على البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parables render meanings like concrete persons; sensory things are firmer in the mind than subtle abstractions, so the comparison clarifies them.
rows.anchor: فإن الأشخاص والأعيان أثبت فى الأذهان لاستعانة الذهن فيها بالحواس بخلاف المعانى المعقولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A parable works only when its image is familiar and accepted by the listener.
rows.anchor: ولا ينتظم مقصود التشبيه والتمثيل إلا بأن يكون المثل المضروب مجربا مسلما عند السامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parables clarify the hidden through the evident and the unseen through the witnessed; images of light and darkness reinforce faith's appeal and disbelief's ugliness.
rows.anchor: فالمرغب فى الإيمان مثلا إذا مثل له بالنور تأكد فى قلبه المقصود والمزهد فى الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parables also rebuke opponents; God uses them abundantly in the Qur'an and other scriptures, including a Gospel chapter called Parables.
rows.anchor: وفيه أيضا تبكيت الخصم وقد أكثر تعالى فى القرآن وفى سائر كتبه من الأمثال

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says representation unveils meanings and brings imagined things near to observation; the image's stature follows the subject's, so truth is light and falsehood darkness, while a spider's house shows weakness.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشرى التمثيل إنما يصار إليه لكشف المعانى وإدناء المتوهم من المشاهد فإن كان المتمثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathal means something unusual, and by extension a notable or strange state, attribute, or story; the rock parable is an example of the descriptive use.
rows.anchor: والمثل هو المستغرب قال الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الإمام فخر الدين الرازي
rows.claim: Fakhr al-Din distinguishes mithl, equal in complete essence, from mathal, equal only in an external attribute; this resolves an apparent conflict between denying and affirming likeness of God.
rows.anchor: وفرق الإمام فخر الدين بينهما بأن المثل هو الذى يكون مساويا للشىء فى تمام الماهية

rows.speaker: حازم
rows.claim: Hazim says proverbs follow customary patterns or use rare departures to prepare the soul, warn against avoidable harm, encourage proper aims, and explain unlikely events; 2:264 is among the examples.
rows.anchor: وقال حازم فى كتاب منهاج البلغاء وأما الحكم والأمثال فإما أن يكون الاختيار فيها بجرى الأمور على المعتاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks why some examples compare things without naming the subjects, unlike the explicit contrasts in 35:19–22.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت فى بعض هذه الأمثلة تشبيه أشياء بأشياء لم يذكر فيها المشبهات وهلا صرح بها

rows.speaker: ابن بابشاذ
rows.claim: Ibn Babshadh says the definite article of specific reference concerns what is established in external entities, while the generic article concerns what is established in the mind; external instances match the mental universal.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن بابشاذ إن تعريف العهد لما ثبت في الاعيان وتعريف الجنس لما ثبت في الاذهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fourth use denotes a universal essence: replacing the article with 'all' preserves its literal sense and entails exhaustive reference; the valid exception in 103:2 and plural description demonstrate this.
rows.anchor: الرابع إن يقصد بها الحقيقة باعتبار كلية ذلك المعنى وتعرف بانها التي اذا نزعت حسن إن يخلفها كل

rows.speaker: صاحب ضوء المصباح
rows.claim: The scope may be genus or species: an article attached to an action marks a species whose name ceases when the action stops, while one attached to a quality marks a lasting genus.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ضوء المصباح ( 3 ) سواء أكان الشمول باعتبار الجنس

rows.speaker: الإمام فخر الدين الرازي ومن تبعه
rows.claim: Fakhr al-Din and his followers deny that a singular noun made definite by alif-lam is general.
rows.anchor: خلافا للامام فخر الدين ومن تبعه في قولهم إن المفرد المحلي بالالف واللام لايعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that denial: the exception in 103:2 proves generality; the thief wording does not prove it by itself, but denotes the essence of theft, applying to every thief across time.
rows.anchor: ولنا الاستثناء في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Scholars disagree whether the definite article on a plural removes its plural force to make it generic and singular, or leaves the plural meaning intact.
rows.anchor: فان دخلت على جمع فاختلف العلماء هل سلبته معنى الجمع ويصير للجنس

rows.speaker: أكثر الفقهاء والأصوليين
rows.claim: Most jurists and legal theorists take reports phrased with kāna, such as 'he used to fast' or 'we used to do,' as indicating repeated continuity; contrary evidence can specify that general implication.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا الباب الحكاية عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بلفظ كان يصوم وكنا نفعل وهو عند اكثر الفقهاء والاصوليين يفيد الدوام

rows.speaker: الصفار
rows.claim: Al-Saffar says whether past kāna entails continuity is disputed; it does not ordinarily mean the state persists now, and he explains the forgiveness phrase as answering a past question and the zina warning by prior recognition.
rows.anchor: وقال الصفار في شرح سيبويه اذا استعملت للدلالة على الماضي فهل تقتضي الدوام والاتصال اولا مسالة خلاف

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: One view attributed to Sibawayh takes divine descriptions with kāna to mean God has always been so.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشجري في اماليه اختلف في كان في نحو قوله

words: إن الكافرين كانوا لكم عدوا مبينا
rows.speaker: ابن الشجري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shajari's second view says kāna places a state in the past but does not prove it ended when the state can extend; enmity may persist, while Jesus' witness ended when he left them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشجري في اماليه اختلف في كان في نحو قوله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view says kāna establishes the predicate in the past but leaves open whether it continues or ends; God's attributes continue.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم يدل على أن خبرها كان موجودا في الزمن الماضي وأما في الزمن الحاضر فقد يكون باقيا مستمرا

rows.speaker: السيرافي
rows.claim: Al-Sirafi says forgiveness and mercy can cease relative to their recipients when those who need them have passed away.
rows.anchor: قال السيرافي قد يرجع الانقطاع بالنسبة للمغفور لهم والمرحومين بمعنى انهم انقرضوا فلم يبق من يغفر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse begins with creatures that crawl on their bellies because they are the most wondrous example of God's power, followed by the two-legged and then four-legged walkers.
rows.anchor: وفيها لطيفة حيث بدأ بالماشي على بطنه فإنها سيقت لبيان القدرة وهو أعجب من الذى بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general phrase about those held by the right hand includes Muslim and non-Muslim women; the later specification of believing bondwomen excludes marriage to nonbelieving bondwomen.
rows.anchor: فهذا عام فى المسلم والكافر ثم بين أن المراد المؤمنات بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 17:72 the first aʿmā is a noun, while the second is comparative, as confirmed by the following 'more astray'; the comparative describes stronger blindness of insight, which can vary.
rows.anchor: فإن الأول اسم منه والثانى أفعل تفضيل بدليل

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr reads the first aʿmā with imāla as a noun and the second without it to distinguish the noun from the comparative.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قرأ أبو عمرو الأول بالإمالة لأنه اسم والثانى بالتصحيح ليفرق بين ما هو اسم

rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi says patience here most likely means endurance through hardships, since the following verses praise those who endure calamity and are killed in God's path.
rows.anchor: قال البيهقي فى شعب الإيمان الأشبه أن المراد بالصبر ها هنا الصبر على الشدائد لأنه أتبع مدح الصابرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second mode of clarification is supplied elsewhere: the wording 'Master of the Day of Judgment' is explained in 82:17–19 by the day when no soul can act for another and judgment belongs to God.
rows.anchor: الثانى أن يكون بيانه منفصلا عنه فى السورة معه أو فى غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the revelation is one, the blessed night in 44:3 is the Night of Decree in 97:1, not mid-Shaʿban; he also cites the related good-deed wording in al-Naml and al-Qasas.
rows.anchor: وبينه فى سورة الدخان بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited division after 4:172 supplies an omitted contrasting group: those who do not disdain worship or act arrogantly, alongside those who do.
rows.anchor: أي ومن لا يستنكف ولا يستكبر بدليل التقسيم بعده بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mention of four directions in Iblis's threat and of two directions from which messengers came stands for the omitted directions as well.
rows.anchor: فاكتفى هنا بذكر الجهات الأربع عن الجهتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' reply to Pharaoh implicitly adds that Pharaoh did not enslave Moses himself: the reproach was for enslaving the Israelites.
rows.anchor: نعمة تمنها علي أن عبدت بني إسرائيل

words: إِنِ ٱمْرُؤٌا۟ هَلَكَ لَيْسَ لَهُۥ وَلَدٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inheritance phrase 'has no child' implies that the deceased also has no father, since a father would exclude the sister who receives half.
rows.anchor: إن امرؤ هلك ليس له ولد

words: فَأَمَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because ammā divides an implicit summary into at least two groups, 28:67 leaves the opposite group unstated: those who do not repent, believe, or act righteously are not successful.
rows.anchor: فأما من تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا فعسى أن يكون من المفلحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 3:7 the group of the firmly rooted in knowledge is supplied as the other side of the division beginning with those whose hearts deviate.
rows.anchor: فأما الذين في قلوبهم زيغ

words: فَبَدَّلَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ قَوْلًا غَيْرَ ٱلَّذِى قِيلَ لَهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers changed both the prescribed word and deed: they said ḥinṭa instead of ḥiṭṭa and crawled in rather than entering prostrate; the intended plea was forgiveness of sins.
rows.anchor: أي وفعلا غير الذي أمروا به لأنهم أمروا بشيئين بأن يدخلوا الباب سجدا وبأن يقولوا حطة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says the repeated negation is intended without restating every counterpart: mentioning the first terms lets them stand for the omitted second terms.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية دخول لا على نية التكرار كأنه قال ولا الظلمات ولا النور ولا النور والظلمات

words: لَّا يَقْدِرُونَ عَلَىٰ شَىْءٍۢ مِّمَّا كَسَبُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author classifies reversed ordering across parallel passages as a frequent pattern resembling return of the ending to the beginning; here 2:264 places 'anything' before 'of what they earned,' while 14:18 reverses them.
rows.anchor: لا يقدرون على شيء مما كسبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation distinguishes the two bāʾs: in the verse it marks recompense and may accompany a voluntary gift, whereas in the hadith it marks causation, without which the effect cannot occur.
rows.anchor: والثاني أن الباء في الموضعين مدلولها مختلف ففي الآية باء المقابلة وهي الداخلة على الأعراض

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some reverse the distinction, taking the verse's bāʾ as causal and the hadith's as recompense.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من عكس هذا الجواب وقال الباء في الآية للسببية وفي الحديث للعوض

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says no one is saved by deeds, including him, unless God envelops him in mercy, resolving the apparent contrast between deeds and salvation.
rows.anchor: وقد جمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The six-day creation wording appears to leave one day for no creation; reports placing creation's start on Sunday and Adam's creation last on Friday fit if Adam is excluded, while the report that creation began Saturday conflicts unless Adam is excluded from what was between heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى مخبرا عن خلق السماوات والأرض وما بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording in 3:7 does not prove that the Qur'an has only two categories; the Qur'an explains what was sent down, while ambiguous verses are not expected to be clarified and clear ones do not depend on clarification.
rows.anchor: قيل ولا يدل على الحصر في هذين الشيئين فإنه ليس فيه شيء من الطرق الدالة عليه

rows.speaker: الحسين بن محمد بن حبيب النيسابوري
rows.claim: One position reported by al-Naysaburi says the entire Qur'an is muhkam, citing 11:1.
rows.anchor: وقد حكى الحسين بن محمد بن حبيب النيسابوري في هذه المسألة ثلاثة أقوال

rows.speaker: الحسين بن محمد بن حبيب النيسابوري
rows.claim: A second position reported by al-Naysaburi says the entire Qur'an is mutashabih, citing 39:23.
rows.anchor: وقد حكى الحسين بن محمد بن حبيب النيسابوري في هذه المسألة ثلاثة أقوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author accepts the third position as correct: the Qur'an contains both clear and ambiguous verses, as 3:7 states.
rows.anchor: والثالث وهو الصيح أن منه محكما ومنه متشابها لقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhkam derives from restraint or prevention: to make something firm is to prevent it, as a judge prevents wrongdoing and a bridle restrains a horse.
rows.anchor: فأما المحكم فأصله لغة المنع تقول أحكمت بمعنى رددت ومنعت والحاكم لمنعه الظالم من الظلم

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Al-Farisi analyzes the passage as two conditions with one response: it must answer ammā, since ammā cannot lack a response, and cannot answer both conditions; Ibn Malik and Sibawayh follow this analysis.
rows.anchor: قال الفارسي قد اجتمع هنا شرطان وجواب واحد فليس يخلو اما ان يكون جوابا لاما أو لان

rows.speaker: سيبويه وابن مالك
rows.claim: Sibawayh and Ibn Malik also assign the response to ammā.
rows.anchor: وتابعه ابن مالك في كون الجواب لاما وقد سبقهما اليه امام الصناعة سيبويه

rows.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
rows.claim: A later critic denies that this is a true condition interrupting another: the second condition and its response can themselves function as the first condition's response, with an omitted 'whatever the case may be.'
rows.anchor: ونازع بعض المتاخرين في عد هذه الآية من هذا قال وليس من الاعتراض أن يقرن الثاني بفاء الجواب لفظا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author concludes ammā's response is not omitted: part of it is preposed before its fāʾ, as with 'as for the orphan, do not oppress'; the fāʾ of in is dropped to avoid two consecutive fāʾs.
rows.anchor: فتخلص ان جواب اما ليس محذوفا بل مقدما بعضه على الفاء فلا اعتراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 90:17, thumma marks the higher rank of faith relative to freeing and feeding, not later timing; the verse also adds believers' mutual counsel to patience and mercy.
rows.anchor: دخلت لبيان تفاوت رتبة الفك والاطعام من رتبة الايمان إلا إن فيها زيادة تعرض لوصف المؤمنين

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another cited explanation takes thumma to mark the great distance between disbelief and God's creation of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: وذكر غيره في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari uses 'then be guided' after repentance, faith, and righteous action as another example of thumma's rank-marking use.
rows.anchor: وعلى ذلك جرى الزمخشري في مواضع كثيرة من الكشاف كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says thumma marks steadfastness after professing faith as a distinct, higher and better station, not a later event.
rows.anchor: قال كلمة التراخي دلت على تباين المنزلتين دلالتها على تباين الوقتين في جاءني زيد ثم عمرو

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the second thumma in the repeated curse as making the second denunciation more emphatic than the first.
rows.anchor: قلت الدلالة على إن الكرة الثانية من الدعاء ابلغ من الاولى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says thumma magnifies the Prophet's status: following Abraham's way was the noblest honor and greatest blessing given to Abraham, and is granted to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating thumma as rank or distance rather than strictly chronological delay removes the objection that it must mean 'and' in these passages.
rows.anchor: واعلم انه بهذا التقدير يندفع الاعتراض بان ثم قد تخرج عن الترتيب والمهلة وتصير كالواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He offers 78:37 as a similar example of an ending related to its preceding subject; the excerpt does not supply the earlier comparison.
rows.anchor: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما الرحمن

words: ومن يتوكل على الله فإن الله عزيز حكيم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending 'God is Mighty and Wise' fits the command to trust: at Badr roughly 314 believers faced about a thousand polytheists, and God answered hypocrites who said their faith had deluded them and strengthened believers.
rows.anchor: فمناسبة الجزاء للشرط أنه لما أقدم المؤمنون وهم ثلاثمائة وبضعة عشر على قتال المشركين وهم زهاء ألف

words: وَإِن مِّن شَىْءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ
rows.speaker: صاحب الفنون
rows.claim: If creation's glorification means signs and blessings that should prompt reflection, human failure to notice them merits reproach; God's forbearance and forgiveness excuse this neglect.
rows.anchor: أجاب صاحب الفنون بثلاثة أوجه أحدها إن فسرنا التسبيح على ما درج فى الأشياء من العبر

rows.speaker: صاحب الفنون
rows.claim: If animals literally glorify in their own languages, they praise without sin while humans disobey; the closing appeal to forbearance and forgiveness therefore concerns human disobedience.
rows.anchor: أجاب صاحب الفنون بثلاثة أوجه أحدها إن فسرنا التسبيح على ما درج فى الأشياء من العبر

rows.speaker: صاحب الفنون
rows.claim: A third explanation links the ending to the opening assertion that heavens and earth glorify God, and to 42:5, where angels glorify and seek forgiveness for earth's people; the verse can thus cover neglected reflection and forgiven disobedience.
rows.anchor: أجاب صاحب الفنون بثلاثة أوجه أحدها إن فسرنا التسبيح على ما درج فى الأشياء من العبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed hadith says that without grazing beasts, bowed elders, and suckling children, punishment would be poured down upon people.
rows.anchor: وفى الحديث لولا بهائم رتع وشيوخ ركع وأطفال رضع لصب عليكم العذاب صبا
